sentences.t: Active Infrastructure wants data centers on 362 acres off Evergreen Mills Road, in the part of Loudoun County the county's own plan calls the Transition Policy Area.

Loudoun Now described 3.25 million square feet across ten buildings up to a hundred feet tall, with three electrical substations and a backup power storage building, on 325 acres to be rezoned from Transitional Residential-10 to Industrial Park.
The Loudoun Wildlife Conservancy put it at up to 3.5 million square feet on 362 acres, powered by natural gas hydrogen fuel cells with batteries on site.
The record carries 362 acres, no capacity figure, and marks the project suspended.
The land is not empty.
The northern 150 acres is farmland; the southern part is thirteen parcels of the Spring Valley subdivision, ten to seventeen acres each, with single family houses on them.
Inside the area stand a Victorian style house of about 1880, a springhouse, a treehouse and a family cemetery.

The conservancy's objection is the woods: mature forest on the banks of Goose Creek, next to the rural policy area and near the county's only nature preserve, and 325 acres of the Transition Policy Area gone.
It argued no reduction in emissions could offset cutting down carbon-storing forest and destroying that habitat.
The county's own planners opposed the rezoning, calling it a fundamental departure from transitional residential policy and noting the nearest industrial zone is 2.3 miles away.
Planning commission vice chair Michael Turner was blunter: "We have no business building data centers in the Transition Policy Area. It's the wrong place and the wrong time."
On July 23, 2026 the commission voted unanimously to recommend refusal, following county staff, after a record number of speakers and written comments against it.
The application is still moving through the development process.
Fifty data center sites are recorded in Loudoun County, more than in any other county on this map.
Within six kilometres of this parcel sit STACK's Evergreen Mills site, Google's Ashburn campus, Microsoft's Growth Mindset site at Sterling, CyrusOne at Broadlands and two Compass sites.
The 766 megawatt Potomac Energy Center is seven kilometres away.
Loudoun has no moratorium; the nearest rules are Warrenton's ban, Fairfax County's limits from September 13, 2024 and Prince William County's from March 4, 2026.

unconfirmed: The two accounts differ on acreage, 325 against 362, and on square footage, 3.25 million against 3.5 million. No megawatt figure has been published and our record holds none. Reporting that Loudoun's board voted 6 to 1 in July to study whether a data center moratorium would even be lawful comes from a page that could not be opened.

sentences.t: BlackChamber Group, a Washington private equity firm set up in 2019 to buy land and build data centers in Northern Virginia, paid $64 million on November 19, 2021 for 37.6 acres at the junction of Crosstrail Boulevard and the Washington and Old Dominion Trail near Leesburg, in Loudoun County.
That is $1.70 million an acre.
The plan is three two storey buildings of 233,800 square feet each, 701,400 square feet in all, each drawing between 30 and 60 megawatts.
The record carries 38 acres, marks the project proposed, and holds no capacity figure.
The site sits in the densest data center market anywhere.
Fifty data center sites are recorded in Loudoun County.
Vantage's VA3 is two kilometres from here, Google's Leesburg and Ashburn campuses three, STACK's Compass Creek site three, and two Compass sites four.
The 766 megawatt Potomac Energy Center is two kilometres off, and the next generation of any size is fifteen kilometres away in Maryland.
What is changing around it is the county's appetite.

On July 23, 2026 Loudoun's planning commission voted unanimously to recommend refusing Active Infrastructure's Spring Valley Technology Park, a 362 acre campus on Evergreen Mills Road, after a record number of speakers and written comments against it.
County planners had called that rezoning a fundamental departure from transitional residential policy.

Loudoun itself has no moratorium, and the nearest rules are in other jurisdictions: Fairfax County's limits from September 13, 2024, Prince William County's from March 4, 2026, Montgomery County's moratorium from June 12, 2026 and Warrenton's outright ban.

unconfirmed: Whether the three buildings have been built is unknown; the account here dates the purchase to 2021 and does not give a construction date. Reporting we could not open indicates Loudoun's planning commission denied a substation needed to power the approved Tuscarora Crossing buildings, leaving the decision with the board of supervisors; that is not carried above. No water figure or tenant has been published.

sentences.t: MESH Capital LLC wanted three data centers of 150,000 square feet each on 57.42 acres near Route 460 and Cabin Field Road, in the Concord district of Campbell County.
The record carries 57 acres and marks the project cancelled.
Residents told the supervisors to refuse it.

They raised noise and light running without a break, water use they put at more than a million gallons a day, traffic on a dangerous stretch of road, blasting from a rock quarry nearby, and years of construction.

Bill Carson, who lives on Cabin Field Road, said: "I think that our quality of life would be greatly disrupted by this extended construction of a data center. Once built, a data center will produce noise pollution in the form of a constant hum."
Ashby Smith, who owns the adjoining property, said: "The only reason that they haven't put this thing up here already is because that proffer is in place."
Only thirteen adjacent owners had been notified, six of whom do not live on Cabin Field Road permanently, which residents said had kept people out of the process.
The supervisor for the district was not persuaded either.

Matt Cline, the Concord district supervisor, said the ground was wrong and the infrastructure was not there: "There are better heavy industrial sites in the county, if the county wanted a data center, than this one. We should be looking at those areas instead of somewhere that currently has no infrastructure for it and a lot of local residential properties."
A board meeting was set for October 7 at six in the evening.
This is the only data center site recorded in Campbell County.
The nearest other entry is a 300 megawatt Avaio Digital Partners proposal, 19 kilometres away.
Amherst County brought in zoning limits on data centers on June 5, 2026.
The generation nearby is small: the 51 megawatt Altavista biomass plant 36 kilometres off and an 80 megawatt solar farm 38.

unconfirmed: The date of the refusal and the vote are not in the page we read, which was written before the October 7 meeting; our record marks the project cancelled but we could not confirm when or by what margin. No megawatt figure or tenant was published. Who is behind MESH Capital LLC is unknown.

sentences.t: A data center is proposed on 64 acres at 14901 Dumfries Road, Manassas, in Prince William County.
The record names no developer, holds no capacity figure, and gives two sources, a link into the county permit portal and a property records page.

In March 2024 the Prince William board of supervisors let Parsons Business Park build taller, 85 feet instead of 75, on 90 acres at 14237 and 14209 Dumfries Road, and rezoned a further six acres at 7901 Six Towers Road from agricultural to heavy industrial.
Kenny Boddye, Deshundra Jefferson, Margaret Franklin, Victor Angry and Yesli Vega voted for it.
Vega said: "I am comfortable to say that this application checks all of the boxes."
Bob Weir, of Gainesville, voted against on grid grounds: "People are really starting to understand the grid, the demand and the kind of power issues we're dealing [with]."
Amazon Data Services bought that 91 acre site the following month, April 2024, for $218 million, and holds it as land secured for future development.
Eighteen data center sites are counted in Prince William County.

Parsons Business Park is three kilometres from this parcel, CloudHQ's two Manassas campuses twelve and thirteen, and three AWS Manassas sites fourteen to sixteen, two of them operating and one under construction.
Prince William County wrote zoning limits on data centers on March 4, 2026.
Dumfries Road sits 16 kilometres from both the 645 megawatt Possum Point gas plant and the 98 megawatt Covanta Fairfax waste plant.

unconfirmed: No applicant, building count, square footage or power figure was found for this parcel in any page that would open. Three kilometres away is a site that has already been through the process, and it is what this stretch of Dumfries Road is becoming. Reporting in the Prince William Times, which refused requests, describes the Mid-County Industrial Park as 64 acres taking in the 23 acre Colchester Industrial Park on Dumfries Road, planned for at least three data centers, on land between Minnieville Road and the county landfill; none of that is carried above.

sentences.t: Amazon owns 91 acres at 14237 and 14209 Dumfries Road in Manassas, in Prince William County, zoned for data centers and not yet built on.
The record files it under the name of the landowning company, Parsons Business Park LLC, with no developer.
Amazon Data Services bought the land in April 2024 for $218 million, and the site is recorded as land secured for future development rather than a working facility.
The zoning approval that made that possible came the month before, in March 2024, and put the property inside the county's Data Center Opportunity Zone Overlay District.
The record carries 91 acres, marks it proposed, and holds no capacity figure.
The March decision was about height.
The board of supervisors let buildings here reach 85 feet instead of 75, and rezoned another six acres at 7901 Six Towers Road from agricultural to heavy industrial.
Kenny Boddye, Deshundra Jefferson, Margaret Franklin, Victor Angry and Yesli Vega voted for it, and Bob Weir of Gainesville against.
Vega said: "I am comfortable to say that this application checks all of the boxes."
Weir's objection was the grid: "People are really starting to understand the grid, the demand and the kind of power issues we're dealing [with]."
Eighteen data center sites are counted in Prince William County.
The Mid-County Industrial Park parcel is three kilometres away, CloudHQ's Manassas campuses nine and ten, and three AWS Manassas sites twelve to thirteen.
The county wrote zoning limits on data centers on March 4, 2026, two years after this approval.
The 98 megawatt Covanta Fairfax waste plant is 18 kilometres off and the 645 megawatt Possum Point gas plant 19.

unconfirmed: No building count, square footage, megawatt figure or construction date has been published for the Amazon site, and our record holds none. Our 91 acres matches the sale; the WTOP account of the height approval says 90. Whether anything has been built since April 2024 is unknown.

sentences.t: An operating data center of four acres stands at 1755 Old Meadow Road in McLean, Fairfax County, known as the Roosevelt Building.

The building houses Lumen's McLean data center, listed in the building as Level 3 McLean, which the interconnection directory Inflect gives as the single operator there, alongside six service providers and four cloud providers, with Lumen, Zayo, Comcast, Verizon, Fiberlight and Cogent among the carriers.
The record files the entry under Yosemite DC Assets LLC, sourced to a Fairfax County planning report and a county property assessment page.
This corner of McLean is thick with them.
A Northrop Grumman site and the entry recorded as ELIAS DC ASSETS share these coordinates, Valo Park is two kilometres away and a second Northrop Grumman site six.
Inflect places DataBank's IAD2 a tenth of a mile off, at 1764A Old Meadow Lane, which is the address the record files under the ELIAS DC ASSETS name.
Sixteen data center sites are counted in Fairfax County.
The county changed its rules after these buildings went up.
Fairfax County's board of supervisors adopted a data center zoning amendment on September 10, 2024, effective the next day, revising where data centers are permitted and to what standard.

Across the river Montgomery County wrote zoning limits on January 12, 2026 and a moratorium on June 12, Prince George's County a moratorium on July 7, Prince William County limits on March 4, 2026, and Warrenton a ban from July 1, 2025.
The nearest generation of any size is the 766 megawatt Potomac Energy Center, 33 kilometres away.

unconfirmed: No floor area, power draw or construction date for this building was established from a page that would open; directory listings give the Lumen facility as about 62,900 square feet with 15,500 of raised floor and 1.8 megawatts, which were not treated as sources. Searches on the address, the company name and Fairfax County's data center records produced directory listings and no reporting. Who Yosemite DC Assets LLC is, and how it relates to Lumen, is unknown.

sentences.t: Powhatan County's board of supervisors voted 3 to 2 on October 28, 2024 to rezone land and grant a conditional use permit for a data center campus west of Richmond.
The approved ground is 119.9 acres partly bordering Chesterfield County, with three data centers totalling 1.525 million square feet, six supporting buildings, and about 24 acres left as open space.
County staff put the investment at $2.7 billion at full build; the developer said $3 billion.
The developer is Province Group, of Newport Beach, California.
The record carries 180 acres, 2,400 megawatts, and marks the campus under construction.
The campus would draw about 300 megawatts at full capacity, supplied by Dominion Energy.
Getting it there means roughly eighteen months of distribution line work, about three years to expand a substation and about four years to build new transmission line.
The recorded figure of 2,400 megawatts is eight times the number in the approval, and no source supports it.
The case for it was the tax bill.
A study by Mangum Economics put direct county tax revenue at $17 million a year by 2034, rising to $21.5 million counting indirect activity, with 165 direct jobs.
Supervisor Mark Kinney put the obvious question about that figure, noting "the $17 million is projected, and that's if all three buildings are built out," and asking what comes after the if.
This is the only data center site recorded in Powhatan County.
A Google project the record calls Loch is four kilometres away, Upper Magnolia Green East ten, and Tract's Goochland site eleven.
No moratorium applies, and the nearest generation is a 57 megawatt battery installation 18 kilometres off.

unconfirmed: Our record's 2,400 megawatts and 180 acres do not match the approval, which covers 119.9 acres at about 300 megawatts, though a second 60 acre parcel was approved earlier and the two together are marketed as a 180 acre park. Water use and the tenant are unpublished. Whether construction has actually started, as our status says, was not established.

sentences.t: The data center rezoning at Upper Magnolia Green is on the western part of the site, and the eastern part, which is where the record puts this entry, is being turned into a nature preserve.

On Wednesday, May 28, 2025 the Chesterfield County board of supervisors rezoned nearly 980 acres at 4200 Moseley Road and the land adjoining it for data centers, part of more than 1,300 acres rezoned that day for two projects.
Tract A, about 870 acres, is restricted to data centers and related uses; Tract B, about 100 acres, to offices, laboratories, pharmaceutical manufacturing and research.

A separate proposal would make the eastern parcel, between Westerleigh Parkway and Duval Road where new school buildings are going up, a Swift Creek Preserve conservation area of at least 350 acres, taking away the residential development already approved there.
The record holds the eastern part as a proposed data center of 744 acres at 18100 Duval Road, with no developer and no capacity figure.
The conditions attached to the western rezoning are unusually specific.
Buildings are capped at 110 feet, with a minimum 200 foot buffer around Tract A and a 750 foot setback from the existing houses on Moseley Road.
Noise is capped at 75 decibels between six in the morning and eight at night, and 65 decibels overnight.

Supervisor Mark Miller was categorical about the water: "We're never, ever going to put at risk our water as a result of a data center. We have one of the most extensive water proffers in place to ensure that we are walking into this with our eyes wide open."
Vernon McClure, president of Main Street Homes, said not enough had been done about visibility and noise for the homes planned at his Dogwood Creek project.
The board approved a second campus the same day, 350 acres of mostly undeveloped land at 750 Watkins Centre Parkway near Westchester Commons, also restricted to data centers.
Six data center sites are counted in Chesterfield County.
The Province Group campus at Powhatan is ten kilometres away and a Google project the record calls Loch eleven.
Chesterfield has written no moratorium and no zoning limit on data centers.
The nearest generation is a 57 megawatt battery installation 19 kilometres off, then the 386 megawatt Chesterfield plant at 34.

unconfirmed: Our record files this entry as a proposed data center on the eastern part of Upper Magnolia Green, at 18100 Duval Road on 744 acres. The reporting puts the data center rezoning on the western part, at 4200 Moseley Road, and describes the eastern parcel between Westerleigh Parkway and Duval Road as the proposed Swift Creek Preserve, a conservation area of at least 350 acres that removes residential development rather than adding a data center. Whether our entry is a misfiling of the western project, or a separate eastern proposal not in either report, was not resolved, and neither acreage matches our 744. No operator was publicly identified in the reports read and our record names none; reporting elsewhere attributes the rezoning to Google and describes a cap of 1.755 million gallons of public water a day, which could not be confirmed from a page that would open. No megawatt figure or construction date has been published.

sentences.t: This is a small edge building, and the operator is clear about what it is for.

EdgeConneX's Norfolk data center at 3800 Village Avenue, which it calls NOR01, is 19,619 square feet with 4,623 square feet of raised floor, built to take 20 kilowatts and more per cabinet and over 600 watts per square foot.
It sits within four miles of downtown Norfolk and three of the airport, and connects to Allied Telecom, Cloudflare, Cox, Lumen, Lumos, Ninja-IX, Verizon, WhiteSky, Windstream and Zayo.
The company describes it as purpose built to deliver content and applications to local consumers with the lowest possible latency.
The entry puts it on five acres, operating, under EdgeConnex and Warehouse 888 LLC, with no capacity figure, and its only source is a Norfolk city property record.
Set against the campus rezonings elsewhere in Virginia, the scale of this one is the point.
This is one building of under 20,000 square feet inside a city, not a rezoning of several hundred acres.
It is the only data center site recorded in Norfolk.
The nearest others are the two cable landing stations at Virginia Beach, 22 kilometres away, one of them at 25 megawatts.
Suffolk adopted a moratorium on data centers on June 18, 2026.
The 325 megawatt Elizabeth River gas plant is 12 kilometres away, with three solar farms between 19 and 40 kilometres out.

unconfirmed: The power capacity is not published by the operator; directory listings give figures ranging from 0.75 megawatts to a 10 megawatt expansion ceiling and put the building at 100,100 square feet, none of which matches the operator's own 19,619, and we did not treat those listings as sources. The year it was built and the identity of Warehouse 888 LLC are unestablished. No opposition to it has been reported.

sentences.t: Menlo Digital, a California company, is behind a four building data center campus on 74 acres at 2255 Jamestown Drive in Petersburg.
The plan is 1.2 million square feet served by a 300 megawatt substation, and the record's 104 megawatts is what the site is expected to support at full build.
The site plan had been submitted but not approved: county comments went back in late April 2026 and the company had not resubmitted by the time the documents were reported.
An earlier version of the proposal showed two buildings with over a million square feet between them.
The company has been marketing it as a Richmond Virginia data center coming soon.
None of the Petersburg projects needed a public hearing.
The city amended its zoning code in 2024 to allow data centers by right in its M-1 light industrial and M-2 heavy industrial districts, which removed the requirement for anything meeting those terms.
When the documents were reported in July 2026, most of the city council had not heard of the projects.
Ward 4 councilman Charlie Cuthbert said: "I had no clue about any of this until 12 noon today."
Mayor Samuel Parham said he learned of three of the four from the article: "I read about them in the news."
Four data center sites are counted in Petersburg, and three are within six kilometres of this one.
NuVu's campus shares these coordinates, Wagner Properties' is three kilometres away and the Warrenton Group's six.
The 378 megawatt Hopewell Cogeneration plant is 11 kilometres off and the 386 megawatt Chesterfield plant 19.
Petersburg has no moratorium, and since 2024 it has had no hearing requirement either.

unconfirmed: Our record marks the campus proposed, and the reporting has the site plan still awaiting resubmission after county comments in April 2026, with no evidence of construction found. No water figure or tenant has been published. Both Data Center Dynamics reports in our record refuse requests.
